newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt minister says tourism rises in June.
newsitem.headline: Egypt minister says tourism rises in June.

text.p: Egypt's tourism minister was quoted on Friday as saying an unprecedented increase in the number of Arab visitors during June had buoyed year-on-year tourism figures by more than 21 percent.
Mamdouh el-Beltagi said in remarks published in the government-owned al-Ahram newspaper that the number of tourists increased to 298,763 from 246,391 in June 1996.
He attributed the rise to more visitors from Arab countries and the return of British and Russian tourists.
Moslem militant groups seeking to overthrow the government have in the past targeted tourists, but security crackdowns have largely curtailed their activities.
The June figure is lower than numbers quoted by the government's statistics office for May, when 331,000 tourists visited Egypt, but Beltagi said they boded well for the rest of the summer season.
Tourism revenues are one of Egypt's main sources of hard currency. In June 1996, Egypt earned $191 million from the industry. There were no comparative 1997 figures.
